title: Fixed-period fits find no clear 32.761-day chromatic wave in 195 GJ 536 HARPS exposures
abstract: We test the HARPS chromatic index at the reported 32.761-day period of GJ 536 c. Four fixed models give slope amplitudes of 0.274 to 0.709 m/s per unit natural log wavelength. Conditional block sign tests give null tail fractions of 0.673 to 0.960. The main 30-day model gives a slope amplitude of 0.377 and a tail fraction of 0.91975. Under a linear wavelength-slope model this is a 0.099 m/s velocity difference amplitude between 500 and 650 nm, with a nominal upper scale of 0.646 m/s. This scale is not a strict physical limit. Simulated 1 m/s differences are detected in 93 to 96 percent of main-model trials. A rotation-period CRX check also gives no clear signal and fails as a positive control. The data do not establish a planet or exclude nearly achromatic or evolving stellar effects. There is no independent confirmation of the chromatic result. The package has original code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and external retrieval steps. No source records are bundled.

display.caption: Fixed-period chromatic slope tests. The left panel shows the modelled velocity difference scale and the 30-day error radius. Negative endpoints are not physical amplitudes. The right panel shows conditional null tail fractions. All models give no clear wave.

citations.reason: Source, nuisance design and reduction-difference context. This work instead tests CRX.
Earlier time-transfer test of the velocity wave. Our test uses a different response on the same spectra.
